opportunities.title: NOAA NESDIS Broad Agency Announcement FY2027-2028 (rolling; foreign/international organizations eligible)
opportunities.funder: U.S. Department of Commerce - National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), National Environmental Satellite, Data, and Information Service (NESDIS)
opportunities.deadline_text: Applications must be submitted to Grants.gov up to 11:59:59 p.m. Eastern Daylight Time September 30, 2028. ... Applications will be considered on a continuing/rolling basis as they are received. Funding opportunity is subject to the availability of funds.
opportunities.funding_text: "There are no funds specifically appropriated by Congress for this BAA. Funding for potential projects in this notice is contingent upon the availability of appropriations in the fiscal years applicable to the application." No award floor/ceiling stated (Grants.gov lists ceiling/floor 0).
opportunities.duration: "Applications should generally be submitted for a one-year award period, but this may be negotiated if the application is recommended for funding." Anticipated start generally six months after receipt.
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Eligible applicants may be institutions of higher education, nonprofits, commercial organizations, international or foreign organizations or governments, state, local, and Indian Tribal governments. Eligibility also depends on the statutory authority that permits NOAA to fund the proposed activity. CESU projects restricted to non-federal CESU partner institutions.
opportunities.eligible_countries: Not specified (no country restriction stated; foreign organizations explicitly eligible).
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: LEAD: yes - the NOFO explicitly lists 'international or foreign organizations or governments' as eligible applicants, so CIAT (international org, Colombia) or Bioversity (Italy) can apply directly and be funded, subject to NOAA having statutory authority for the specific activity and to SAM.gov UEI + Grants.gov + eRA Commons registration. SUBAWARDEE: also possible under a U.S. lead (subawards follow 2 CFR 200 cost principles). Caveat: this is a non-competitive-discretionary BAA with no dedicated appropriation; success depends on finding a NESDIS program office willing to fund. Duration generally 1 year (negotiable), so it is not a multi-year staff-funding vehicle unless negotiated.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: Single organization applicant with SAM.gov UEI, Grants.gov and eRA Commons registration (Signing Official + PD/PI accounts).
opportunities.geographic_restrictions: None stated; project must address NOAA mission areas.
opportunities.cofunding_details: "Cost sharing is not required unless it is determined that a project can only be funded under an authority that requires matching/cost sharing funds."
opportunities.eligible_activities: "NOAA issues this BAA for extramural research, innovative projects, and sponsorship (e.g., conferences, newsletters, etc.) that address one or more of NOAA's mission areas." Mechanism for activities "not addressed through NOAA's competitive discretionary programs"; not for goods/services for NOAA's direct benefit.
opportunities.required_documents: SF-424 (with eRA Commons PI ID), SF-424A, SF-424B, CD-511, SF-LLL if applicable; 1-page title page; 1-page project synopsis tied to NOAA mission; project description max 15 pages addressing evaluation criteria; literature cited; CVs of key personnel; NOAA NEPA questionnaire (Q1-19 and 51-57); Data Management Plan (up to 2 pages); budget + detailed budget justification; indirect cost rate agreement if charging above de minimis.
opportunities.application_procedure: Submit via Grants.gov (validated through eRA Commons); rolling review as received. Requires SAM.gov UEI, Grants.gov and eRA Commons (organization profile + Signing Official + PD/PI accounts); registration can take 6+ weeks. Title page must name the NOAA Line Office and target program. Contact the Line Office before submitting. NESDIS contact: Olga Dixon (Olga.Dixon@noaa.gov); grants mailbox nesdis.grants@noaa.gov.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: NESDIS covers satellite data/products (e.g., GOES, JPSS/VIIRS, data stewardship). EO-based drought/vegetation monitoring, AI on satellite data and climate data services for agriculture fit methodologically, but NESDIS's mission is weather/environmental satellites rather than agriculture, so the agricultural framing must be built around NOAA products/services.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: One of very few open U.S. federal research vehicles where a foreign/international organization can be the funded lead and salaries are allowable; useful to build a NOAA relationship (e.g., LAC climate services) but unsolicited BAAs have low and unpredictable funding.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Team has strong Sentinel/Landsat/MODIS + ML skills; adapting to NOAA satellite products (VIIRS, GOES) is straightforward. Administrative burden (eRA Commons, NEPA questionnaire) is the main hurdle.
opportunities.recommendation: Pursue opportunistically: only submit after a NESDIS program officer signals interest. Pitch a concrete NOAA-product use case (e.g., VIIRS/GOES-based crop drought early warning or validation of NOAA vegetation/drought products in the Andes/Central America). Do not rely on it for multi-year staff funding; at most a 1-year (negotiable) award.
opportunities.potential_partners: NOAA NESDIS Center for Satellite Applications and Research (STAR) scientists; U.S. universities with NOAA cooperative institutes (e.g., CISESS/U. Maryland, CIRA/Colorado State) as co-investigators.
opportunities.next_action: Email Olga.Dixon@noaa.gov / nesdis.grants@noaa.gov with a 1-page concept to identify a sponsoring NESDIS program; in parallel confirm CIAT's SAM.gov UEI status and eRA Commons registration.

opportunities.title: Feed the Future Innovation Labs (U.S. Department of State, 8 labs announced 2026-10-15) - funded sub-recipient pathway for international research centers
opportunities.funder: U.S. Department of State - Office of Global Food Security
opportunities.program: Feed the Future Innovation Labs, DFOP0017826 (Assistance Listing 19.017); Title XII of the Foreign Assistance Act
opportunities.deadline_text: Prime competition closed: "Concept Note Application deadline: April 9, 2026". Awards announced October 15, 2026. No deadline for partner/sub-recipient engagement has been published; any sub-award calls would be issued by the individual labs.
opportunities.funding_text: "Individual awards may range from a minimum of $20 million to a maximum of $40 million (approximately) over the life of the award." "$64 million total in FY 2026 (with outyear funding subject to the availability of funds)". Amounts are per lab (prime award), not per sub-recipient; sub-award sizes Not specified.
opportunities.duration: "Length of performance period: Up to 60 months"; "Anticipated project start date No later than September 30, 2026".
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Prime: "Applications must only be submitted by eligible U.S. colleges and universities as defined under Section 296(d) of Title XII of the Foreign Assistance Act". Partners: "All types of U.S. and non-U.S. entities are eligible as collaborating partners (i.e. sub-recipients or contractors at various tiers)".
opportunities.eligible_countries: Activities in low- and middle-income countries (World Bank classification) aligned with U.S. foreign-policy goals; specific lab countries Not specified in the release.
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: LEAD: no (prime restricted to U.S. Title XII universities; prime competition closed). FUNDED PARTNER: yes - the SOI states non-U.S. entities are eligible as sub-recipients or contractors 'at various tiers', provided they are not excluded in SAM.gov, and it explicitly describes the labs as collaborating with 'national and international research centers'. CIAT/Bioversity can therefore receive sub-awards from the lead universities. Most relevant labs for the Alliance: Coffee and Cacao (U. Hawaii; LAC relevance), Sustainable Intensification of Targeted Agricultural Systems - SITAS (Kansas State), Cereals (Kansas State), Fertilizer and Soil Health (Auburn), High Value Crops - SAFE (U. Florida). Whether a given lab already includes CGIAR partners is Not specified.
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: U.S. Title XII-eligible college/university (land-grant, sea-grant, or other U.S. universities with agricultural research/extension capacity).
opportunities.geographic_restrictions: LMICs; geographic targeting must align with U.S. National Security Strategy and State Department Agency Strategic Plan 2026-2030.
opportunities.consortium_details: Labs are university-led multi-partner programs: "multiple partners, principal of which are U.S. universities, working in collaboration with scientists in developing country universities, national and international research centers, the private sector, and non-governmental organizations". No required percentage of funding for sub-awards (Q&A Answer 25).
opportunities.cofunding_details: "Cost sharing or matching is not required."
opportunities.eligible_activities: Objective 1: productivity, sustainable intensification, soil/water management, resilience to weather shocks, pests/pathogens, breeding, livestock/animal health. Objective 2: nutrition, food systems, food safety. Cross-cutting: "Use of a range of innovations and advances, including Artificial Intelligence and digital solutions"; "Coordination and collaboration with the global agricultural research community, including global research institutions".
opportunities.required_documents: For partners: Not specified (determined by each lead university's sub-award process; must be registered/not excluded in SAM.gov).
opportunities.application_procedure: No open application for partners. Engage directly with the Management Entity (lead university) of each lab; sub-awards are made under 2 CFR 200.331/200.318-200.320 procedures per Q&A Answer 25.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Climate-resilience, sustainable intensification and AI/digital decision support for smallholders are explicit themes, but the labs are crop/commodity-centred; RS/crop-modelling would be a service component within lab research portfolios.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Main surviving U.S. government channel for international agricultural research after USAID's dismantling; up to 5-year programmes; Coffee & Cacao lab directly relevant to Colombia/LAC; State Dept has also directly funded a CGIAR center (CIMMYT, USD 40M, Feb 2026).
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Alliance has deep coffee/cacao, soils, digital agriculture and EO capacity in LAC, Africa and Asia; feasibility depends on lab partner selection.
opportunities.recommendation: Partner-only (ineligible as lead). High priority to contact lab directors now while awards are starting up (start no later than 30 Sep 2026; 60-month horizon), offering EO/crop-model/digital advisory services and LAC field networks, especially to the Coffee & Cacao (U. Hawaii) and SITAS/Cereals (Kansas State) labs. Coordinate with Alliance/CGIAR partnership office.
opportunities.potential_partners: University of Hawaii (Coffee and Cacao); Kansas State University (Cereals; SITAS); Auburn University (Fertilizer and Soil Health); University of Florida (High Value Crops - SAFE); University of Georgia (Peanut); Washington State (Animal Health); Mississippi State (Fish).
opportunities.next_action: Identify Management Entity directors of the Coffee & Cacao, SITAS and Cereals labs (university websites) and send a partnership note; confirm CIAT/Bioversity active SAM.gov registration.

opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: FUNDED LEAD: no. UNFUNDED: CIAT could be a non-U.S. PI/Co-I on a no-exchange-of-funds basis, contributing in-kind (field data, crop models, LAC/Asia networks) to a U.S.-led proposal whose U.S. team is funded. Does NOT fund CIAT staff. Included only for strategic value (land-cover/land-use and agriculture EO science networks).
opportunities.lead_applicant_requirements: U.S. institution for funded proposals; registration in NSPIRES.
opportunities.cofunding_details: Non-U.S. participants must self-fund their contribution.
opportunities.eligible_activities: Not specified until ROSES-27 is released (ROSES-25 Earth science elements included A.4 Rapid Response, A.14 Atmosphere, A.15 Biosphere, A.16 Cryosphere, A.17 Hydrosphere, A.18 Geosphere).
opportunities.application_procedure: Via NSPIRES once ROSES-27 elements are released; many Earth science elements use mandatory Step-1 proposals or NOIs.
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: NASA biosphere/LCLUC and applied-science agriculture elements match RS/ML crop and land-use work directly, but exact ROSES-27 element content is unverified.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Access to NASA science teams and data products; no funding for CIAT staff.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Team can contribute in-kind EO/crop-model expertise and ground data.
opportunities.recommendation: Do not count as staff funding. Monitor ROSES-27 release (by Jan 2027) and offer CIAT as an unfunded collaborator to U.S. PIs (e.g., NASA Harvest-linked universities) where it adds data access or co-authorship value.
opportunities.potential_partners: U.S. universities active in NASA LCLUC/Harvest (e.g., University of Maryland), U.S. SERVIR science team members.
opportunities.next_action: Watch the NASA ROSES page and NSPIRES in Dec 2026-Jan 2027; identify U.S. PIs planning biosphere/land-use proposals.

opportunities.title: NIH Fogarty GEOHealth - Hubs of Interdisciplinary Research and Training in Global Environmental and Occupational Health (RFA-TW-28-001, forecast)
opportunities.funder: U.S. National Institutes of Health (NIH) - Fogarty International Center (FIC)
opportunities.deadline_text: Forecast: "Estimated Application Due Date: Sep 22, 2027"; estimated synopsis posting Apr 22, 2027; estimated award/project start Jul 20, 2028.
opportunities.eligible_applicants: Forecast applicant types: public and private institutions of higher education; nonprofits with or without 501(c)(3) status. Foreign-organization eligibility Not specified in the forecast.
opportunities.eligible_countries: Collaboration between U.S. and LMIC scientists required ("include collaboration between U.S. and LMIC scientists").
opportunities.cgiar_eligibility_notes: Unclear until the NOFO is published (est. Apr 2027). Past GEOHealth rounds (RFA-TW-21-001) used a U01 award to an LMIC institution linked to a U2R award to a U.S. institution (per FIC programme page), which would suggest CIAT (Colombia-based) could be the LMIC institution - but this could not be verified for the new RFA, and NIH's 2025 foreign-subaward policy (NOT-OD-25-104) now uses linked foreign awards. Treat as potential funded LMIC partner/lead pending NOFO. Topic must be environmental/occupational exposures and health (e.g., heat/pesticide exposure of agricultural workers, wildfire smoke), not agriculture per se.
opportunities.consortium_details: "GEOHealth awards will 1) include collaboration between U.S. and LMIC scientists, 2) include closely aligned components for research and research training".
opportunities.eligible_activities: Environmental and occupational health research plus research training; address environmental/chemical exposures and their health impacts; data sharing; training of graduate students, postdocs and early-career investigators.
opportunities.application_procedure: Not specified until NOFO (NIH ASSIST/Grants.gov; requires eRA Commons).
opportunities.scientific_alignment_rationale: Climate and health is adjacent; EO/climate data for exposure assessment (heat, smoke, agro-chemicals) could be a component, but the core must be health research.
opportunities.strategic_relevance_rationale: Multi-year hub format with research training; would require a health-research lead partner; outside the Alliance's core mandate.
opportunities.technical_feasibility_rationale: Requires health/epidemiology leadership the team does not have.
opportunities.recommendation: Low priority. Monitor NOFO release (~Apr 2027); pursue only if a Colombian or U.S. health research partner wants EO/climate exposure expertise. Alternative NIH route: PA-26-002 (Collaborative International Research Project, PF5) allows funded linked foreign awards under a U.S. prime, but also requires an NIH health mission focus.
opportunities.potential_partners: Universidad del Valle / Universidad de Antioquia public health schools; U.S. schools of public health with LAC environmental-health programmes.
opportunities.next_action: Set a reminder for April 2027 to read the NOFO eligibility section (foreign/LMIC institution rules).
